paper.title: Algorithm 939: Computation of the Marcum Q-function

stack: Fortran 90 (netlib CALGO 939.zip: Fortran90/Src cons.f90, incgam.f90, marcumq.f90, constants; Fortran90/Drivers testmarq.f90 and outputQP.dat; Doc/Makefile)

claim.text: Reference DATA array q, element 5, in Fortran90/Drivers/testmarq.f90 (inside 939.zip): Q_8(13, 15) = 0.8516869957363, the Marcum-Q value at mu = 8, x = 13, y = 15. Registered by scout from the artifact's own reference data. Tolerance 1e-10 absolute, fixed before any run.

attempt: G1: the archive's Makefile (Doc/Makefile), unchanged, fails in the sandbox: it names g95 (absent) and expects the sources beside it, but the archive ships them in Fortran90/Src and Fortran90/Drivers, so make stops at 'No rule to make target cons.f90'. Patch (build-only): the same Makefile run with FC = the sandbox gfortran 16.2.0 and VPATH pointing at the archive's Src and Drivers, objects in a separate build directory. The shipped driver prints only relative errors, so impl/valq8.f90 (new code, outside the archive) calls the authors' marcum(8, 13, 15) and prints the value. No archive file is edited. Two passes: the recipe ran twice from a fresh unpack.

original_attempt.reason: make: no rule to make target 'cons.f90' (the archive's Makefile in Doc/ expects its sources beside it; the archive ships them in Fortran90/Src and Drivers). g95, the Makefile's default compiler, is also absent from the sandbox (checked with command -v).

evidence: evidence/recipe-run.log (first run: the build passed, the record step refused the patch as source, kind source, record_exit 2; cause: the build commands were not literal text in the recipe)
